name: Heydar Aliyev International Airport
before:
Azerbaijan's main airport and the busiest in the South Caucasus, 20 km north east of Baku on the Baku Airport Highway. It is the hub for Azerbaijan Airlines and for the cargo carriers Azal Avia Cargo and Silk Way West.

Terminal 1 is where a client will almost certainly be. It handles international flights and the bulk of the traffic, with 40 check in desks, 24 passport control positions, 15 gates and twelve air bridges, two of them built for the A380. Terminal 2 takes domestic and short range flights.

Terminal 1 is worth seeing rather than just passing through. Arup designed it in 2010 in a three cornered shape under a semi transparent roof, and the Turkish practice AUTOBAN filled the interior with a series of oak veneer cocoons. There are five lounges and a spa.

It was commissioned in April 2014 and is built for 6 million passengers a year, currently running at up to 3 million, with parking for 600 cars.

The airport was formerly called Bina International, after the suburb it stands near.
after:
Baku's airport, about 20 km north east of the city. It handled 7.5 million passengers in 2024, up 31 per cent. Azerbaijan Airlines is the main airline, and the cargo carrier Silk Way West has its hub here.

International flights mainly use Terminal 1, opened in April 2014, which has 40 check in desks, 24 passport desks, 15 gates and 12 air bridges. Arup engineered the triangular building and the Turkish studio Autoban lined it with wooden cocoons clad in oak veneer. There are several lounges.
